In detail

Bogenhausen is one of Munich's 25 official Stadtbezirke (city districts). Polizeipraesidium Muenchen and the Statistisches Amt Muenchen recorded 2,818 total offences here in 2025, across a population of 95,475 residents (31 December 2024) — a rate of 2,952 offences per 100,000 residents, roughly 0.6x the citywide average, below it. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central, station, or nightlife-heavy district can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential district can show a low rate simply by having few offences relative to its population. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Munich — real Polizeipraesidium Muenchen / Statistisches Amt Muenchen figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Bogenhausen safe?

Wandroz currently rates Bogenhausen in Munich, Germany as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Munich, Germany, based on Polizeipräsidium München / Statistisches Amt München's 2025 recorded-offence data. This source has no time-of-day breakdown, so this is one overall level rather than a separately measured day and night figure — see the note on this page before treating the day/night badges as independently measured.

Does Bogenhausen's rating cover night-time safety specifically?

Not separately. Polizeipräsidium München / Statistisches Amt München's 2025 recorded-offence data publishes one figure per zone with no time-of-day split, so Bogenhausen's day and night badges show the same underlying level rather than an independently measured night figure. Treat it as a general indicator, not a night-specific measurement.

Is Bogenhausen a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Bogenhausen's rating is a useful general indicator, but this data is normalised against registered residents, not visitor footfall — busy tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher without that meaning elevated risk for a visitor passing through.
